title: 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI Guideline for Coronary Artery Revascularization & 2014 AHA/ACC NSTEMI Guideline

definitions.STEMI: ST-elevation MI: new ST elevation ≥1mm in ≥2 contiguous leads, or LBBB
definitions.NSTEMI: Non-ST-elevation MI: troponin elevation without ST elevation criteria
definitions.TIMI Risk Score: 0–7 point score for NSTE-ACS; ≥3 = high risk
definitions.GRACE Score: Predicts in-hospital and 6-month mortality in ACS

recommendations.text: Primary PCI is the preferred reperfusion strategy for STEMI when it can be performed within 120 minutes of first medical contact.
Fibrinolytic therapy should be administered within 30 minutes of STEMI diagnosis when PCI cannot be performed within 120 minutes.
Aspirin 162–325 mg loading dose is recommended for all patients with ACS as soon as possible.
Dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor or prasugrel preferred over clopidogrel) is recommended for patients with ACS managed with PCI.
High-intensity statin therapy should be initiated or continued in all patients with ACS.
Beta-blockers should be initiated within 24 hours in patients with STEMI without signs of HF, low-output state, or contraindications.
ACEi or ARB should be initiated within 24 hours in STEMI patients with anterior MI, HF, or LVEF <40%.
MRA should be prescribed in STEMI patients with LVEF ≤40% and HF symptoms or DM already receiving ACEi and beta-blocker.
Early invasive strategy (within 24h) is recommended in NSTE-ACS patients with elevated troponin, new ST depression, GRACE score >140, or refractory symptoms.
Immediate invasive strategy (within 2h) is recommended for NSTE-ACS with refractory angina, haemodynamic instability, or ventricular arrhythmias.
Cardiac rehabilitation is recommended for patients with ACS.
DAPT for 12 months following ACS with PCI is recommended (shorter if bleeding risk outweighs benefit).
For patients with ACS and AF requiring anticoagulation, triple therapy (OAC + DAPT) should be limited to the shortest necessary period; dual therapy (OAC + P2Y12) preferred thereafter.

pharmacotherapy.examples: aspirin 162–325 mg load, then 75–100 mg daily
ticagrelor 180 mg load → 90 mg BID; prasugrel 60 mg load → 10 mg daily; clopidogrel 600 mg load → 75 mg daily

pharmacotherapy.indication: All ACS — LDL target <70 mg/dL or ≥50% reduction
Post-ACS LDL ≥70 mg/dL on maximally tolerated statin

key_trials.name: PLATO
key_trials.finding: 16% RRR in CV death/MI/stroke vs clopidogrel post-ACS

key_trials.name: TRITON-TIMI 38
key_trials.finding: 19% RRR in CV death/MI/stroke vs clopidogrel, more bleeding

key_trials.name: FOURIER
key_trials.finding: 15% RRR in MACE with PCSK9i added to statin post-ACS/ASCVD

key_trials.name: ODYSSEY-OUTCOMES
key_trials.finding: 15% RRR in MACE; reduced mortality in patients with LDL ≥100

key_trials.name: DANAMI-3-PRIMULTI
key_trials.finding: Multivessel PCI in STEMI reduces MACE vs culprit-only

key_trials.name: ISCHEMIA
key_trials.finding: Routine invasive strategy not superior to conservative in stable CAD

ecg_criteria.STEMI: ≥1 mm ST elevation in ≥2 contiguous limb leads OR ≥2 mm in ≥2 contiguous precordial leads OR new LBBB
ecg_criteria.posterior_STEMI: ST depression ≥1 mm in V1–V4 with upright T; confirmed by V7–V9
ecg_criteria.RV_STEMI: ST elevation in V4R; usually RCA occlusion
